clue.text: Expedition heading for Surtsey, a distant island

indicators.note: the head of the word Surtsey is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: distant means far

explanation.surface: A trip bound for Surtsey, a remote volcanic island off Iceland.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland expedition, especially one to watch or hunt wildlife in Africa.

clue.text: Seafood fraud private investigator reveals

parts.note: a scam is a fraud or swindle

explanation.surface: A detective uncovers some fishy business in the shellfish trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustines, usually breaded and fried, a classic seafood dish.

clue.text: Snapped after apartment cleaned out

indicators.note: the word for snapped is placed after the word for apartment in the answer

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
snapped means broke

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper after their flat was burgled and stripped bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaned out is slang for having no money left, which is what being flat broke means.

clue.text: One who's pragmatic about top celebrities?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Asks whether a hard-headed person is someone who cares about famous stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist accepts things as they are and acts practically, the essence of being pragmatic.

clue.text: Information, given prior to summit, in contradictory language

parts.note: news is information
a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: News announced ahead of a summit meeting, phrased in doublespeak.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspeak is the deliberately ambiguous, self-contradictory official language of Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Veteran suffered

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, veteran means long practised
to have ... something painful is to have suffered it

explanation.surface: An old soldier who went through hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Experienced means both seasoned like a veteran and having undergone or suffered something.

clue.text: Extend prison term

definitions.meaning: slang for a spell in jail

explanation.surface: Lengthen a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch as a verb means lengthen; as a noun it is criminal slang for a period served in jail.

clue.text: Select English, low in calories

parts.note: lite is the marketing spelling for a low-calorie product

explanation.surface: Choosing an English diet product.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective means choice or exclusive, as an elite group is.

clue.text: Very much involved, want to enter tower

indicators.note: the word for want goes into the word for tower, entering it

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
to want is to need

explanation.surface: Someone longs to get inside a castle tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knee-deep in something means being deeply immersed or heavily involved in it.

clue.text: Film a vessel joining a river

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids

explanation.surface: A movie about a boat joining a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container, VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 science-fiction film, one of the highest-grossing films ever.

clue.text: A couple of pianos increase in value

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano (softly), so two of them make PP
to raise is to increase

explanation.surface: A pair of pianos goes up in worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'value' here is the verb, to assess worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of something, to value it.

clue.text: Well-known short novel, Rider's first for Longmans'

definitions.note: Longmans' stands for Longmans is, a publishing house

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: public means well known, openly known
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: the first of Rider's means its opening letter alone

explanation.surface: A famous novella by H. Rider Haggard, his first for the publisher Longmans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims PUBLIC to PUBLI. 'Rider' points to H. Rider Haggard, whose She was published by Longmans; 'novel' gives SHE. Longmans' is read as Longmans is.
explanation.definitionFit: Longmans was a long-established London book publishing house.

clue.text: Very scary, shock increasing

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it, so shock gives hair
raising means increasing

explanation.surface: A frightening jolt that keeps getting stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like fright but is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hair-raising is terrifying, enough to make your hair stand on end.

clue.text: Tense, small daughter finds river

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
wee means small

explanation.surface: A nervous little girl comes upon a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river forming part of the border between England and Scotland.

clue.text: Away team risk a long shot

parts.note: out means away, not at home
a side is a team
to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: A visiting team takes a gamble that is unlikely to come off.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a slim possibility, a long shot unlikely to succeed.

clue.text: Wistfulness may be shown by lots again in resort

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Revisiting a holiday resort leaves many feeling wistful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in resort' looks like a seaside town but means re-sorted, the anagram signal for LOTS AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is sentimental longing for the past, a form of wistfulness.

clue.text: Science, principally, reportedly grabs students

indicators.note: principally points to the principal, leading letter of Science
reportedly means the word that follows is heard rather than seen spelt

parts.note: to collar someone is to grab or seize them

explanation.surface: Science, according to reports, mainly attracts learners.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholars are learned people or pupils, students in the broad sense.

clue.text: Best nuts and biscuits

parts.note: the cream is the best part, the pick
crackers means mad, nuts

explanation.surface: Top-quality nuts and biscuits on a snack tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food beside biscuits but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream crackers are plain, crisp, savoury biscuits popular in Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Actress, having stitch in side, retired

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole assembled word is read backwards
in places the word for stitch within the word for side

parts.note: a side is a team
to stitch is to sew

explanation.surface: An actress gets a stitch in her side and withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes TSEWEAM, which 'retired' then reads backwards, splitting differently into the actress's two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Mae West was an American stage and film actress famous for her innuendo.

clue.text: Boffin, for example, good leader

parts.note: a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A clever scientist as a good boss, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a brainy scientist; egghead is a similar term for an intellectual.

clue.text: Visit a nurse following onset of tetanus

indicators.note: following means the word for nurse comes after the first letter of tetanus
the onset of a word is its beginning, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Go and see a nurse after tetanus sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event or place is to go to it, to visit.

clue.text: Express a point of view over coniferous tree

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: Someone holding forth about a conifer.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion.

clue.text: Leaders in Israel did address head of state

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their initial letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Israeli leaders spoke to a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' reads as one phrase, but 'head of' are fodder and 'state' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Put out when mine is swallowed by bar worker

indicators.note: being swallowed means going inside, so the word for mine sits within the word for bar

parts.note: an inn is a bar or pub
a dig is an excavation, a mine
a worker ant, so ant stands for worker

explanation.surface: A barmaid annoyed when her drink is downed by a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a possessive but is a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Put out means annoyed or offended, as an indignant person is.

clue.text: Of theoretical interest only, relating to a college education?

definitions.meaning: a point that is ... has no practical relevance
to do with colleges and scholarly learning

explanation.surface: Something that matters only in theory, like a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic means both scholarly, of colleges, and irrelevant in practice, as a moot point is.

clue.text: Black bird dog

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a bird

explanation.surface: A dark bird dog, the kind used in hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird dog' reads as one term for a gundog, but bird is EAGLE and dog stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound bred for hunting hares.

clue.text: Brief period in deficit

parts.note: brief means short
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A short spell in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack, an amount falling short, a deficit.

clue.text: King's wife in dread at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A king's wife fearful on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward is the name of several English kings.
